passage:
When Ruby cleaned her father's desk, she found an old movie ticket. The date on it was twenty years ago.
Her father smiled when he saw it. "That was the first movie your mother and I watched together," he said.
The ticket was small and yellow. The words were almost gone. Ruby asked why he kept it for so long.
Her father said, "Because a small piece of paper can hold a large memory."
Ruby thought about all the things she threw away without thinking: birthday cards, bus tickets, notes from friends. That night, she put a shoebox under her bed and named it "Memory Box."
She did not want to keep everything. She only wanted to give some small things a chance to become important later.
